hints: Focus on which functional groups actually react with sodium to release hydrogen gas.
Remember that 1 mol of an -OH group or a -CO2H group gives only 0.5 mol of H2, so count the acidic hydrogens in each option.
Look for the molecule that has two reactive hydrogens in total, as that is what you need to make a full mole of H2 from one mole of Y.
walkthrough:
**Recall how sodium makes hydrogen**

Sodium is a strong reducing agent that reacts with acidic protons. Both alcohols and carboxylic acids react to give hydrogen gas.

Chemical equation rule:
$$2\text{RO-H} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{RO-Na} + \text{H}_2$$
$$2\text{RCO}_2\text{-H} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{RCO}_2\text{-Na} + \text{H}_2$$

**Work out the mole ratio**

Notice from the equations that 2 mol of -OH or -COOH gives 1 mol of H2. That means 1 mol of a group gives only 0.5 mol of H2.

Key rule:
$$1 \text{ mol acidic H} \rightarrow 0.5 \text{ mol H}_2$$

**Apply to 1 mol of Y**

We are told 1 mol of Y makes 1 mol of H2. Using the ratio above, Y must contain 2 mol of acidic hydrogens per molecule.
$$\text{moles H}_2 = \frac{\text{number of -OH plus -CO}_2\text{H groups}}{2}$$

**Count groups and conclude**

Options A, B and C each have only one reactive group, so they give only 0.5 mol H2. Only $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CO}_2\text{H}$ has both an alcohol $\text{-OH}$ and a carboxylic acid $\text{-CO}_2\text{H}$, giving 2 acidic H and therefore 1 full mol of H2.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ is butan-1-ol with only one -OH group. 1 mol gives only 0.5 mol H2, not 1 mol.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_3\text{COH}$ is a tertiary alcohol with only one -OH group. Like any simple alcohol, 1 mol gives only 0.5 mol H2.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ is butanoic acid with only one -CO2H group. Although acids are more reactive, 1 mol still gives only 0.5 mol H2.
options.D: Correct. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CO}_2\text{H}$ is lactic acid and has two acidic protons, one from the alcohol -OH and one from the carboxylic acid -CO2H. Both react with Na, so 1 mol of Y gives 2 x 0.5 = 1 mol of H2.
